public.text: This is the correct position and the chapter does not address the strategic risk it creates. Broad semantic harmonisation across all domains is both the most expensive element of a national programme and the element most exposed to automation: normalising free text, mapping between code systems and reconstructing context from surrounding documentation are precisely the tasks language models are improving at. Countries reading this chapter may commit to the costliest and least robust part of the agenda.
public.suggestedRevision: Distinguish what is robust under any AI trajectory from what is a bet on one. A small mandatory provenance set - source, method of measurement, time and status - is robust, because no model can reconstruct what was never recorded: whether a blood pressure was taken at home or in clinic, whether a diagnosis was a working hypothesis or a conclusion, whether a value was later revised. Broad semantic harmonisation is a bet. Recommend mandating the first, sequencing the second behind it, and setting an explicit review point. International estimates differ by more than an order of magnitude between countries that connect to existing standards and countries that model afresh, which makes this the largest single cost decision in a national programme.
